message.content:
`contenteditable` is a *special* attribute that accepts three string values: | Value | Meaning | |-------|---------| | `"true"` | The element is editable. | | `"false"` | The element is not editable. | | `"plaintext-only"` | The element is editable, but only plain text can be entered (no formatting). | So when you receive the value **`"plaintext-only"`**, you should use that exact string as the attribute value. It is already a valid value for `contenteditable`; you do **not** need to convert it to `"true"` or `"false"`. **Example** ```html
This text can only be plain text.
``` If you’re writing a helper that normalizes values, you can simply return the input unchanged when it is `"plaintext-only"`. Only the strings `"true"` and `"false"` should be converted to their boolean equivalents if you need a boolean flag in your code.
